title: Our prophets did all this and more
source_text: Ἡ μὲν Πυθία ἱστόρηται ὅτι καὶ νοθευθεῖσα ἔχρησέ ποτε· οἱ δὲ παρ᾿ ἡμῖν προφῆται οὐ μόνον ὑπὸ τῶν κατ᾿ αὐτοὺς ἐθαυμάσθησαν διὰ τὴν ἐνάργειαν τῶν λεγομένων ὑπ᾿ αὐτῶν ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἑξῆς χρόνοις. ἐκ γὰρ ὧν ἔχρησαν οἱ προφῆται καὶ πόλεις ὠρθώθησαν καὶ ἄνθρωποι ὑγιάσθησαν καὶ λιμοὶ ἐπαύσαντο. ἀλλὰ καὶ εἰς ἀποικίαν σαφῶς τὴν ἀπ᾿ Αἰγύπτου εἰς τὴν Παλαιστίνην κατὰ χρησμοὺς ἐλήλυθεν ὅλον τὸ Ἰουδαίων ἔθνος· ὅπερ μετελθὸν μὲν τὰ προσταχθέντα ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ εὐδαιμόνησε σφαλὲν δὲ μετέγνω. τί δὲ δεῖ λέγειν ὅσοι δυνάσται καὶ ὅσοι ἰδιῶται κατὰ τὰς ἱστορίας τῆς γραφῆς ἄμεινον ἢ χεῖρον προσέχοντες ταῖς προφητείαις ἢ ἀμελήσαντες ἀπήλλαξαν; εἰ δὲ καὶ περὶ ἀπαιδίας δεῖ λέγειν, ἐφ᾿ ᾗ δυσφοροῦντές τινες γεγόνασι πατέρες ἢ μητέρες, τὰς περὶ τούτου εὐχὰς ἀναπέμψαντες τῷ τῶν ὅλων δημιουργῷ, ἀναγνώτω τις τὰ περὶ τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ καὶ τῆς Σάῤῥας, ἐξ ὧν γέγονεν Ἰσαὰκ ἤδη γεγηρακότων. ὁ παντὸς τοῦ Ἰουδαίων ἔθνους πατὴρ καὶ ἑτέρων παρὰ τούτους. ἀναγνώτω δὲ καὶ τὰ περὶ Ἰεζεκίου, οὐ μόνον ἀπαλλαγὴν νόσου λαβόντος κατὰ τὰς Ἡσαΐου προφητείας ἀλλὰ καὶ τεθαῤῥηκότως εἰπόντος τό· „ἀπὸ γὰρ τοῦ νῦν παιδία ποιήσω. ἃ ἀναγγελεῖ τὴν δικαιοσύνην σου.“ καὶ ἐν τῇ τετάρτῃ δὲ τῶν Βασιλειῶν ἡ ὑποδεξαμένη τὸν Ἐλισσαῖον, χάριτι θεοῦ προφητεύσαντα περὶ γενέσεως παιδὸς, κατὰ τὰς εὐχὰς τοῦ Ἐλισσαίου γέγονε μήτηρ. ἀλλὰ καὶ πηρώσεις ἰάθησαν μυρίαι ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ. καὶ ἄλλοι πρὸς τῷ ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἱερῷ τολμήσαντες ὑβρίσαι τὴν Ἰουδαϊκὴν θρησκείαν πεπόνθασι τὰ ἀναγεγραμμένα ἐν τοῖς Μακκαβαϊκοῖς.
pass_a_gloss: The Pythia (Πυθία) is recorded (ἱστόρηται) to have given oracles (ἔχρησε) once even when corrupted/bribed (νοθευθεῖσα); but the prophets among us were marvelled at (ἐθαυμάσθησαν) not only by those of their own time (κατ᾿ αὐτούς) because of the evidentness (ἐνάργειαν) of the things said by them but also in the following times. For from what the prophets gave as oracles (ἔχρησαν) both cities were set upright (ὠρθώθησαν) and men were made healthy (ὑγιάσθησαν) and famines ceased (ἐπαύσαντο). But also to a colony (ἀποικίαν) clearly, the one from Egypt to Palestine, according to oracles (κατὰ χρησμούς) the whole nation of Jews went; which, pursuing (μετελθόν) the things commanded by God, prospered (εὐδαιμόνησε), but having stumbled (σφαλέν) repented (μετέγνω). What need to say how many rulers and how many private persons, according to the histories (ἱστορίας) of Scripture (γραφῆς), fared better or worse attending (προσέχοντες) to the prophecies or neglecting them? And if one must also speak about childlessness (ἀπαιδίας), at which some being grieved became fathers or mothers, having sent up (ἀναπέμψαντες) prayers (εὐχάς) about this to the creator of the universe (τῷ τῶν ὅλων δημιουργῷ), let one read the things about Abraham and Sarah, from whom, already grown old (γεγηρακότων), Isaac was born, the father of the whole Jewish nation and of others besides them. And let him read the things about Hezekiah, not only receiving release (ἀπαλλαγήν) from disease according to the prophecies of Isaiah but also saying boldly (τεθαῤῥηκότως): for from now on I will make (ποιήσω) children (παιδία), who will announce (ἀναγγελεῖ) your righteousness (δικαιοσύνην). And in the fourth of the Kingdoms (Βασιλειῶν) the woman who received (ὑποδεξαμένη) Elisha, who prophesied by the grace (χάριτι) of God about the birth of a child, according to Elisha's prayers became a mother. But also countless (μυρίαι) maimings (πηρώσεις) were healed by Jesus. And others, daring (τολμήσαντες) at the temple in Jerusalem to outrage (ὑβρίσαι) the Jewish worship (θρησκείαν), suffered the things recorded in the Maccabean books (Μακκαβαϊκοῖς).
pass_b_english: The Pythia is recorded to have once given oracles even after she had been bribed. But our prophets were admired for the clear truth of what they said, not only by the people of their own day but in later times as well. For through the oracles the prophets gave, cities were restored, men were made well, and famines came to an end. Indeed, the whole nation of the Jews plainly went out as a colony from Egypt to Palestine in keeping with oracles; when it carried out what God commanded, it prospered, and when it went astray, it repented. Why need I tell how many rulers and how many private persons, according to the histories of Scripture, fared better or worse by heeding the prophecies or neglecting them?

And if we must speak of childlessness too, and of those who, distressed at it, became fathers or mothers after sending up their prayers about it to the Maker of the universe, let anyone read the story of Abraham and Sarah, from whom Isaac was born when they were already old (Genesis 21:1–7), the father of the whole Jewish nation and of others besides. Let him read also the story of Hezekiah, who not only gained release from his illness in keeping with the prophecies of Isaiah (Isaiah 38:1–8), but also said with confidence: “For from now on I will beget children, who will declare your righteousness” (Isaiah 38:19). And in the second book of Kings, the woman who received Elisha, after he had prophesied by the grace of God that a child would be born, became a mother in answer to Elisha’s prayers (2 Kings 4:8–17).

Besides, countless maimings were healed by Jesus. And others who dared, at the temple in Jerusalem, to outrage the Jewish worship suffered what is recorded in the books of the Maccabees (2 Maccabees 3:24–28).

choices.choice: Origen answers Celsus’s list in 45 item by item and reuses his words: cities ‘restored’ (ὠρθώθησαν), famines, the ‘colony’, ‘carried out what was commanded’ and ‘prospered’, rulers and private persons ‘fared better or worse’, childlessness, maimings ‘healed’, and outrage at the temple. The English keeps the same words as in 45. χρησμοί / ἔχρησαν are rendered ‘oracles’ to keep the parallel with Celsus. νοθευθεῖσα (‘corrupted’) is taken as ‘bribed’; Herodotus tells of the Pythia being bribed (5.63, by the Alcmaeonids; 6.66, by Cleomenes against Demaratus), but Origen does not say which story he means, so no inline source is given. Isaac is ‘father of the whole Jewish nation and of others besides’, i.e. also of Esau’s descendants. Hezekiah’s healing is told in Isaiah 38:1–8 and 2 Kings 20:1–11; Isaiah is cited because Origen goes on to quote Isaiah’s chapter. The quotation follows the Septuagint of Isaiah 38:19 (‘from today I will beget children, who will declare your righteousness’), which differs from the Hebrew (‘the father makes known to the children your faithfulness’); ‘from now on’ renders the staged ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν (LXX ἀπὸ τῆς σήμερον). ‘Fourth book of Kingdoms’ is the Septuagint name for 2 Kings; kept in the text and cited by its English name. 2 Kings 4 tells of Elisha’s promise to the Shunammite woman; it does not mention a prayer by Elisha for the birth, though Origen speaks of his prayers. ‘In the books of the Maccabees’ renders τὰ ... ἐν τοῖς Μακκαβαϊκοῖς; the clearest case of outrage at the temple being punished is Heliodorus in 2 Maccabees 3:24–28 (see also Antiochus in 2 Maccabees 9). ‘Countless maimings were healed by Jesus’ refers to the Gospel healings generally; no single passage cited. Origen’s ‘others’ (plural) may also take in Alcimus, struck down when he pulled down the wall of the sanctuary court (1 Maccabees 9:54–56), though Origen names the Maccabean books only in general.
Childlessness sentence: added 'and yet' (not in the Greek) removed; now 'and of those who, distressed at it, became fathers or mothers'
'let a man read' changed to 'let anyone read' (ἀναγνώτω τις); inverted 'was born Isaac' put in natural order
Scripture checked: Genesis 21:1–7, Isaiah 38:1–8, Isaiah 38:19 (LXX wording followed), 2 Kings 4:8–17 (= LXX 4 Kingdoms), 2 Maccabees 3:24–28; note added on 1 Maccabees 9:54–56
